content: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Unit. This is Officer Brian Cooper. Who am I speaking with today?
Um, hi, my name is Emily Carter. I got a voicemail saying there's a serious tax problem? I'm really confused.
Yes, Emily, thank you for calling us back. Our records show a discrepancy in your federal income tax filings from the last two years. There are significant irregularities under your name.
Irregularities? I'm not even sure what that means. I just graduated last year. Did I do something wrong with my taxes?
According to the IRS audit, there is an unpaid tax amount along with penalties and overdue interest. The total has reached $3,895.42, and it's increasing daily.
Oh my god, I, I don't have that kind of money. I'm barely making rent. How did this happen?

Emily, I understand this is alarming. But if this situation is not resolved right now, you could face immediate legal action. This includes liens on your bank accounts, wage garnishments, and even a possible arrest warrant.
Wait, arrest? I can't, please, I can't have anything happen to me. My job would fire me. Is this for real?

I sincerely wish I had better news for you. If you do not take care of your IRS obligations today, your account will be escalated to the Federal Claims Court first thing tomorrow, and law enforcement could be notified immediately.
No, please, I just want to fix whatever this is. I don't want to get in trouble. What can I do?
You must settle this balance today to avoid legal consequences. We have arrangements for urgent payments, do you have access to your bank, credit card, or a payment app like Zelle or Venmo?
I have a debit card, but there's not much on it. I have a credit card, but I'm not sure what the limit is.
That's fine. We can split the payment. For security, the IRS now accepts government-approved payment methods, including instant crypto transfers and prepaid gift cards. Which can you manage today?
I guess I could maybe use my credit card or, um, buy a gift card? I'm just really scared right now.

You're doing the right thing, Emily. Please do not discuss this call with anyone, even bank staff, as it could interrupt the compliance process and trigger enforcement. Now, how much can you put on your credit card right now?
I think maybe $1,000. That's all I have left on it.
That's a start. For the remainder, you can purchase three Target or Apple gift cards, each loaded with $1,000. Once you have them, stay on the line and read me the numbers from the back.
Gift cards? Are you sure? Isn't there another way?
Emily, this is the only way to avoid a legal escalation today. If you hesitate or hang up, the system automatically proceeds with asset seizure. Please, I don't want that to happen to you.
Okay, okay, I'll go to Target now. Should I stay on the phone?
Yes, please stay on the line. Do not talk to anyone about this. If a cashier asks, just tell them the cards are for personal use. Let me know when you have the cards.
Alright, I'm heading there now. I'm really nervous. I just want this to be over.
I'll walk you through every step. Once you read me the gift card numbers and make the credit payment, your IRS file will be cleared, and you'll receive a confirmation email. Do you understand?
Yes, I understand. I'll do whatever you say. Please help me.
